A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OW/ISP aggregation work, with readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. The conditional-independence extension in v1 Section 6 is retained in v2 Appendix C, allowing comparison despite reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulations and LLM aggregation experiments on UltraFeedback, MMLU, and ARMMAN, including detailed ensemble results in Appendix E.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds baseline comparisons, robustness evaluations, statistical analyses, and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: OW, ISP, OW-L, and OW-I retain their aggregation rules, objectives, and accuracy-estimation procedures. EOW is relocated from Section 6 to Appendix C without changing its procedure. The new experiments do not introduce a proposed method component.

E1.justification: The synthetic setting and three real-world datasets remain. v2 adds a targeted MMLU-hard evaluation population containing questions where at least two strong models select the same incorrect option. This extends difficult-distractor coverage without adding a new domain or source corpus.

E2.justification: v1's real-world ensemble tables compare the proposed methods principally against MV. v2 Tables 7–9 add Dawid–Skene and SP across all three datasets and all 16 original ensembles; SP previously appeared only in simulations. This substantially broadens the empirical comparator set. Single Best remains reported but is explicitly characterized as an oracle.

E3.justification: Original simulation settings, prompts, filtered dataset sizes, and four-family ensembles are retained. Added evaluations use a specified 13,886-question MMLU subset, all eight models together, and four-model ensembles containing strong and weak variants from two families. These introduce supplementary selection and ensemble protocols rather than revising the original experiments.

E4.justification: New Section 6 and Appendix F.4 substantially expand checks of practical assumptions: per-model option-position bias, concentrated errors on hard distractors, eight-model aggregation, and potentially correlated same-family ensembles. These directly examine robustness beyond the original simulations and cross-family benchmark comparisons.

E5.justification: v1 reports point accuracies without inferential tests. v2 adds paired per-question correctness counts and t-tests, reporting t-statistics of 12.53, 23.39, and 3.22 and p-values below 0.001. Appendix F.3 also newly discloses seed 0 and claims ranking stability across seeds, without specifying repeated-run counts or reporting uncertainty intervals.

E6.justification: Tables 2–3 and all 48 original ensemble-result rows retain their values. Substantial new results cover DS/SP comparisons and robustness settings; for example, MMLU-hard accuracy is 24.79% for OW-L/OW-I versus 17.23% for MV. Section 5.4 also changes the reported fraction of cases where OW-I and ISP beat MV from 85.83% to 95.83%, consistent with the retained tables.

T1.justification: The principal theorems and proofs are retained, including the relocated conditional-independence extension. Example 2 corrects the easy-question parameter from alpha = 1 to alpha = infinity, matching its proof. Section 5.2 additionally asserts convergence of OW-L/OW-I to optimal weights, but the cited Theorem 4.2 concerns ISP's empirical advantage and provides no corresponding convergence proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion broaden the empirical superiority claim from majority voting to standard or other baselines. The introduction also explicitly emphasizes OW-L/OW-I's empirical consistency. The central contributions—Bayesian-optimal OW and label-free second-order aggregation through ISP—remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds explicit acknowledgment of weaker models' position bias and interprets the new stress tests as evidence of robustness beyond theoretical assumptions. It also clarifies Single Best's dependence on unavailable labels, contextualizes gains through remaining error headroom, and explains how the aggregator could complement existing multi-agent pipelines.

D1.justification: Appendix F.3 adds Apple M3 Pro runtime information: UltraFeedback accuracy estimation takes 10.3 seconds for OW-L and 6.1 seconds for OW-I, with approximately 0.1 seconds for subsequent aggregation. The Azure API settings, A100/vLLM setup, prompts, and filtering details were already documented in v1.

R1.justification: v2 adds Dawid and Skene (1979) and positions the methods against classical EM-based aggregation. It also clarifies the distinction from MoE and the complementary relationship to multi-round reasoning pipelines. The broader related-work review in Appendix A.1 is substantially retained.

P1.justification: Most exposition and the main narrative sequence remain, with localized rewrites and expanded explanations. The original Section 6 moves to Appendix C, its main-text position becomes the robustness section, and appendices are renumbered. Conflict-of-interest and impact statements are also added.

P2.justification: The main text changes from single-column to two-column formatting, with revised typography, headers, author presentation, and table placement. v2 adds Tables 4–6 and 10–13 and expands the original ensemble tables with SP and DS columns. Both original figures retain identical image content but are relocated and resized.

improvement.justification: The added DS/SP comparisons and targeted robustness tests make the empirical validation more informative, while runtime disclosures improve practical transparency. These gains are limited by the unsupported convergence assertion in Section 5.2 and unreconciled statistical reporting: Table 10's ARMMAN counts imply approximately 0.59 percentage points of improvement, versus 0.54 in Table 3 using the stated sample size. The revision therefore provides a limited net improvement rather than a substantial increase in evidential reliability.
